sections.title: Putting the unit together
sections.content: You know *no creo que* from B1 Unit 7, *dudo que* from B1 Unit 13, *sino que* from B1 Unit 40 and the polite conditional (*me gustaría*) from A2 Unit 26. In this unit you added the opinion verbs with *no*, the verbs of doubt and denial, *no es que... sino que...* and the possibility markers. Together they give you a way to disagree that is clear but not rude: grant a point, state your doubt, correct the reason, and soften with the conditional.

sections.title: A polite disagreement in four moves
rows: Pero no creo que sea tan sencillo.
No es que me oponga, sino que me faltan datos.
Correct the reason (no es que... sino que...).
Yo no diría que sea un error.
Soften with the conditional diría and the subjunctive.

sections.title: Softening with the conditional
sections.content: *No digo que sea un error* states your view directly. *No diría que sea un error* ('I wouldn't say it is a mistake') is gentler, because the conditional makes it sound like a suggestion. Both take the subjunctive, as other negated verbs of saying and thinking do.

items.spanish: Puede que tengas razón, pero no creo que sea tan sencillo.
items.english: You may be right, but I do not think it is that simple.

items.spanish: Yo no diría que sea un error, pero dudo que sea la mejor opción.
items.english: I wouldn't say it is a mistake, but I doubt it is the best option.

items.spanish: No es que esté en contra de la idea, sino que me faltan datos.
items.english: It is not that I am against the idea, it is that I lack data.

items.spanish: Entiendo tu punto de vista, pero no estoy de acuerdo.
items.english: I understand your point of view, but I do not agree.

sections.content: Disagree with the idea, not with the person. *No creo que eso sea cierto* sounds calmer than *Estás equivocado*. And when the other person has a good point, say so: *Tienes razón en eso*.
